Economic Community and Rural Development Directorate 
 
Tipperary County Council’s Community, Economic, and Rural Development Directorate plays a vital role in fostering 
inclusive growth across the county. The council is committed to ensuring balanced economic and social development 
by focusing on various sectors like local enterprise, rural regeneration, tourism, community services, and sports 
infrastructure.

Tipperary LCDC have held two meetings since the last update. TCC, ERCD section presented an update

FAI 
The following is an update on football initiatives & development by the two FAI Development Officers 
through April and May 2025. 
Club Development 
The FAI Club Mark is a series of accreditation awards for grassroots clubs based on best practice in the 
governance, management and administration of a club and is now mandatory for all clubs to hold at least 
the entry level award by December 31st, 2025.   
Borrisokane FC and Clodiagh Rangers FC obtained the entry level award in May.  
All clubs across the county that do not hold this award are being engaged with and supported. All clubs 
have engaged and are now registered for the award.  Ongoing continuous support is being provided to 
clubs who are in the process including, Garda vetting, safeguarding training, policy development, and 
coaching supports.

women 18+, with no experience necessary. Moneygall, Nenagh Celtic, BT Harps FC and Clonmel Town 
FC continue with their Kick Fit programmes.

TOURISM 
 
 
 
Brand Refresh 
The Time for Tipperary logo has undergone a light refresh — a cleaner, more versatile update that reflects 
how the brand will present across all visitor-facing platforms in the months and years ahead.  
 
New ‘Time for Tipperary’ Merchandise Design 
The Time for Tipperary brand refresh reimagines the county as a distinctive, engaging destination. To 
support this identity, a collection of merchandise concepts has been developed using the refreshed logo, 
colour palette, and a series of evocative message lines, including: Time to unwind; Time to breathe; Time 
to discover; Time to explore, and Time to make memories. These lines are designed to work across a 
wide range of gift items. Tipperary Tourism is engaging with tourism trade currently to bring these ideas 
to life. 
 
Tipperary Discovery Guide 
The new guide features a comprehensive listing of what to see and do across Tipperary, including 
attractions activities, events, family fun, and more. Many listings include QR codes that link directly to up-
to-date digital content. There is a comprehensive distribution plan in place, to ensure it reaches key visitor 
locations throughout the year. 
Tipperary Tourism Strategic Plan 2025-2030 
Consultants have been contracted to collaborate with the Tipperary Tourism company to deliver this 
plan. A draft will be presented to the Board of Tipperary Tourism the first week in June.

Climate & Energy 
 
Mid-Tipperary Decarbonising Zone (DZ) 
In accordance with DZ Action 2.2 of the Climate Action Plan the Council hosted a public 
information event on the 16th April at the TUS Thurles Campus. On the day, a wide range of 
Climate Action and Local Carbon Community service providers helped communities and businesses 
learn how to engage in climate action. Highlights of the day included learning about the Tipperary
